subject: Human Evolution
title: Raw Material Curation
description: A 60-second lesson on Raw Material Curation.

hook.text: Not all rocks are good for tools. Finding the right stone could mean a journey of many days.

buildup.text: Obsidian, flint, and chert fracture predictably. Granite and sandstone don't—they crumble.

discovery.text: Hominins learned which stone types work best and traveled or traded specifically to obtain them.

twist.text: Material preference implies long-term memory, landscape knowledge, and cost-benefit thinking.

climax.text: Choosing the right rock was the first supply-chain decision in history.

punchline.text: Good tools started with knowing good rocks.

quiz.question: Why did early hominins prefer certain rock types?
options: They fracture predictably into sharp edges
